findings.reason: The email.js rewrite throws email-nochange whenever the target equals the profile email, without checking whether that email is verified. New unverified accounts store their email in the profile, so initial confirmation, resending, and ACP forced sending to that address fail; the official socket email-confirmation test also fails. The rewrite leaves confirmByUid rejecting users with no profile email despite the requested fallback, and confirmByCode calls confirmByUid concurrently with writing a newly confirmed email, so confirmation can read the old or missing address.

The header edit calls user.email.emailValidationStatus(req.uid), but the email.js rewrite in step 90 defines no such function. Rendering a header for a logged-in user therefore fails. It also removes isEmailConfirmSent without updating public/src/app.js, which still reads that field to decide whether to offer another confirmation email.

The ACP controller edit calls user.email.emailValidationStatuses(uids), but no implementation of that function was added. Loading the ACP user list or search results therefore throws instead of computing the four required email states.

The ACP template uses conditions such as `<!-- IF users.emailValidationStatus == "validated" -->` without the parentheses required by Benchpress equality expressions; a targeted Benchpress precompile treats this form as literal text rather than a working conditional. The template also references statuses.* translation keys absent from the final patch and tests for `none` while step 103 assigns `no-email` as its fallback. The required four-state display cannot render correctly.

run_review.reason: The completed official evaluation is unresolved: the user socket email-confirmation test fails. The final patch also blocks confirmation emails whenever the requested address matches the profile email, even if that email is unverified; calls undefined status functions from both the logged-in header and ACP user controller; and uses ACP template conditions that Benchpress does not interpret. Core sending and status-display workflows remain broken.

findings.reason: The search for an account edit template ended with inspection of build/public/templates/account/edit.tpl, following the additional account-path probes in steps 35–37. The requested status display was in the ACP, whose source template had already been located and inspected in steps 15 and 20. Proceeding with that template would have avoided this bounded, unused detour.

After the test in step 64 could not connect despite an earlier standalone Redis startup reporting PONG, the agent again started Redis in a separate shell call. Starting it together with the test was the cheaper reasonable response to that evidence; the separate restart added a call without keeping Redis available for the next test.

The agent reran the same email-confirm test in a new shell after only another standalone Redis startup. It again returned ECONNREFUSED, repeating the connection failure from step 64 and consuming another test invocation without new test information. A combined startup-and-test call, later used in step 72, was available.

Having found that the broad `--grep "email confirm"` also selected a test dependent on an earlier fixture, the agent ran all of test/user.js: 173 tests took about 28 seconds before an unrelated invitation test failed. Anchoring the grep to the known `User` → `email confirm` suite would have checked the relevant baseline with substantially less unrelated work.
